Alcohol dehydrates you primarily because it acts as a diuretic by suppressing antidiuretic hormone (ADH), also called vasopressin, causing your kidneys to excrete more water than usual . Without enough ADH signaling your kidneys to reabsorb water back into your bloodstream, more fluid passes out as urine.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESeAHEIkXX-iXgyKIBbsEoZAuNXUsIR5hKnm7dDfxvG9Ljrn3Ozp2azskGYL8gYKHYYAEILrxmdJ9HxKmV1qJbZEO-V5q2lOneuqXwdgAv3Ek92UaNVwmOG93E8yyYxAHIUegZ023Wmh4xRPsnZwNDhhvYkq3e9-BPuw)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfwHEIkXX1vlOmzbkKW8B0s8s3Q3ZA7vZtogxGxitCnMuvJZuWV4L2d4Gup6x0xujSWUshTK3IgEYns62k9EfK9OTvbN2lw1XUp8QyG--qrsMa_ZcOBev-0RTvBJ4Cx0qoPRTnmCMzGGSlEqnifOzxz5a_ESDZ4cHqjUFnFAWtdo)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZQHEIkXXWl5Fi_Ui7Rh4TNeNbIqjEAspp1uEBoSqugZZ8cQJECGOK97qPGHlMatcgTxhaKzXu4fUKSZhMasonqvmPqUSvh7vfcIaCWmw7Rj4PxegpezGA5twrk5f9lRb8xlN150C)

### Key Factors Behind Fluid Loss

- **Increased urination:** Suppressing ADH reduces water retention and increases urine output, which can also deplete electrolytes like sodium and potassium.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfwHEIkXX1vlOmzbkKW8B0s8s3Q3ZA7vZtogxGxitCnMuvJZuWV4L2d4Gup6x0xujSWUshTK3IgEYns62k9EfK9OTvbN2lw1XUp8QyG--qrsMa_ZcOBev-0RTvBJ4Cx0qoPRTnmCMzGGSlEqnifOzxz5a_ESDZ4cHqjUFnFAWtdo)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXXjhKGcih1wSAWBLzsctcnrF-SL4yZdLuzZYcOxC8mXFDVwYYiXiOrBuTVXc1kXwaFb7qAIrpKnI_mJHIIH0x-ybPciA5IrWgfkeMubsnKqwM-vH2z4b0aKn4wY4Zeu7QJXk12dzU3)
- **Sweating and blood vessel dilation:** Alcohol can widen blood vessels and affect autonomic regulation, which may increase sweating and fluid loss—especially in warm environments.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESewHEIkXXk8RPOSdMniHQY4wzBjhJA_A73EGEPn-4gMCsQRejQMdDrUelUK56wS1rzjWpy869GwRMTRtl_3fXm5tS3pOJo0FIXY_2aOdPegiDf-lqLZF0pvvkhgOqNFMqTHOqFVdeUuHRgUGchPNHilgVTl8c9Rt6AC-6wQ)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESeAHEIkXX-iXgyKIBbsEoZAuNXUsIR5hKnm7dDfxvG9Ljrn3Ozp2azskGYL8gYKHYYAEILrxmdJ9HxKmV1qJbZEO-V5q2lOneuqXwdgAv3Ek92UaNVwmOG93E8yyYxAHIUegZ023Wmh4xRPsnZwNDhhvYkq3e9-BPuw)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfgHEIkXXWc3M4xenAJiMTbmkGkPhfeKfh1Z4XG-njd4JsyLw62cMuStKnFiOVwmIVrjssHJCCnhStYCaFO6cKk_di6q6uksN0l--y8jHzShw-n0UOwr-ioxSocPCpxOdooR1LAnXwd5upWlBwKxtA7QKm481RtzW450vR9LgVw)
- **Altered thirst signals & GI effects:** Alcohol can dull thirst cues or cause nausea and vomiting, making it harder to replace lost fluids.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfgHEIkXXWc3M4xenAJiMTbmkGkPhfeKfh1Z4XG-njd4JsyLw62cMuStKnFiOVwmIVrjssHJCCnhStYCaFO6cKk_di6q6uksN0l--y8jHzShw-n0UOwr-ioxSocPCpxOdooR1LAnXwd5upWlBwKxtA7QKm481RtzW450vR9LgVw)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESewHEIkXXk8RPOSdMniHQY4wzBjhJA_A73EGEPn-4gMCsQRejQMdDrUelUK56wS1rzjWpy869GwRMTRtl_3fXm5tS3pOJo0FIXY_2aOdPegiDf-lqLZF0pvvkhgOqNFMqTHOqFVdeUuHRgUGchPNHilgVTl8c9Rt6AC-6wQ)
- **Faster absorption & higher ABV:** Drinking on an empty stomach, drinking quickly, or consuming higher-ABV drinks speeds up alcohol's entry into the bloodstream and intensifies fluid loss.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESeAHEIkXX-iXgyKIBbsEoZAuNXUsIR5hKnm7dDfxvG9Ljrn3Ozp2azskGYL8gYKHYYAEILrxmdJ9HxKmV1qJbZEO-V5q2lOneuqXwdgAv3Ek92UaNVwmOG93E8yyYxAHIUegZ023Wmh4xRPsnZwNDhhvYkq3e9-BPuw)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfwHEIkXX1vlOmzbkKW8B0s8s3Q3ZA7vZtogxGxitCnMuvJZuWV4L2d4Gup6x0xujSWUshTK3IgEYns62k9EfK9OTvbN2lw1XUp8QyG--qrsMa_ZcOBev-0RTvBJ4Cx0qoPRTnmCMzGGSlEqnifOzxz5a_ESDZ4cHqjUFnFAWtdo)

As explained by [Cleveland Clinic](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESeAHEIkXX-iXgyKIBbsEoZAuNXUsIR5hKnm7dDfxvG9Ljrn3Ozp2azskGYL8gYKHYYAEILrxmdJ9HxKmV1qJbZEO-V5q2lOneuqXwdgAv3Ek92UaNVwmOG93E8yyYxAHIUegZ023Wmh4xRPsnZwNDhhvYkq3e9-BPuw) , alternating alcoholic drinks with water, eating food beforehand, and pacing your intake help slow alcohol absorption and limit dehydration. Most users on [Reddit](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESpQEBxCJF1_s7l3FXyIwrhF6kDAzX9LDBRx99EF2n-OsjE7w_9JDqwps4s3rPc8fu2AjwjmGZH9v_X61sMcIXCLWKUunW2e8pmSCk3W6ez7ZlICTXMvCQ1D9ZB-M5lnFSEr4BSRPB71zUDwbcmJE9y8b250hLrA3IfoAKxHCRqk3wKjWAIp9UzG16nL-8_WsuFLclo8f4tUlAl0oXbF4nx81iLLQIoVg) agree that alcohol inhibits ADH in the brain, prompting the kidneys to flush out more water than you might expect from the liquid volume alone.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESeAHEIkXX-iXgyKIBbsEoZAuNXUsIR5hKnm7dDfxvG9Ljrn3Ozp2azskGYL8gYKHYYAEILrxmdJ9HxKmV1qJbZEO-V5q2lOneuqXwdgAv3Ek92UaNVwmOG93E8yyYxAHIUegZ023Wmh4xRPsnZwNDhhvYkq3e9-BPuw)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESpQEBxCJF1_s7l3FXyIwrhF6kDAzX9LDBRx99EF2n-OsjE7w_9JDqwps4s3rPc8fu2AjwjmGZH9v_X61sMcIXCLWKUunW2e8pmSCk3W6ez7ZlICTXMvCQ1D9ZB-M5lnFSEr4BSRPB71zUDwbcmJE9y8b250hLrA3IfoAKxHCRqk3wKjWAIp9UzG16nL-8_WsuFLclo8f4tUlAl0oXbF4nx81iLLQIoVg)Are you looking into **hangover prevention**, **how different drinks compare** , or **specific symptoms** like headaches and dry mouth?
